meanings.note: + genitive. Core Russian prep meaning 'without' in everyday speech.
the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
Present есть; у меня есть = I have. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be; there is'.
future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

+ accusative (where to). Core Russian prep meaning 'in, into' in everyday speech.

meanings.note: The neuter form 'всё' used alone. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Neuter всё. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Plural все. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Внимание! = Attention!. Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'attention' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: А ну-ка, дай посмотрю! Внимание, ребята!
examples.trans: Hold on, let me have a look! Attention, everyone!

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: И, Марина Сергеевна, читайте всё внимательно! Особенно мелким шрифтом!
examples.trans: And, Marina Sergeyevna, read everything carefully! Especially in fine print!

meanings.note: Prefix 'вс-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'егда').

examples.trans: She's offended. She's always like that.

говорить.gloss: to speak, to say, to talk

meanings.note: Я тебе говорю = I'm telling you. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to speak, to say, to talk', paired with 'сказать'.
Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to speak, to say, to talk', paired with 'сказать'.
usually the short form: я готов (m), я готова (f)

Disbelief. Core Russian part meaning 'yes' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: My mood really is very good.

meanings.note: Asks about the purpose. Core Russian adv meaning 'what for, why' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Oh, Samson. What have you come for?

meanings.note: Location. Core Russian adv meaning 'here' in everyday speech.
emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Чн is pronounced шн. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

examples.trans: I need to do a bit of work.

examples.text: Мы даём вам ещё немного времени.
examples.trans: We are giving you a little more time.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'nobody', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Никто не будет командовать на моей кухне!
examples.trans: Nobody is going to give orders in my kitchen!

examples.text: Не говори об этом никому, ладно?
examples.trans: Do not tell anyone about this, okay?
But legally you are nobody to her.

meanings.note: usually in the genitive ничего, with не: ничего не осталось

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.

meanings.note: hesitation, at the start of a sentence
Ну, папа!. Core Russian part meaning 'well; come on' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.en: it is necessary, one needs to
meanings.note: + dative of the person + infinitive: мне нужно позвонить

examples.trans: I need to call the governor. Give me a phone.

meanings.note: + dative of the person: обещать вам

examples.text: Марина, я вам обещаю: со стеной ничего не случится.
examples.trans: Marina, I promise you: nothing will happen to the wall.

meanings.note: Общий туалет = a shared toilet. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('shared, common').

examples.trans: This is a shared bathroom, Vanya!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'one', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Нам очень дорого обходится авторская кухня.
examples.trans: Auteur cuisine costs us very dearly.

examples.text: Это все, кто выходил из отеля.
examples.trans: That is everyone who left the hotel.

meanings.note: Used as an exclamation of approval. Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'лично'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Отлично, Ваня! Вот это твой образ!
examples.trans: Perfect, Vanya! That right there is your look!

meanings.note: With verbs: очень люблю. Core Russian adv meaning 'very, very much' in everyday speech.
With verbs: очень люблю. Core Russian adv meaning 'very, very much' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.

meanings.en: to have a talk, to speak (with someone)
meanings.note: Поговорить с + instrumental. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'говорить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to have a talk', paired with 'говорить'.

examples.text: Поговори с Аракеляном. Пусть он заберёт заявление.
examples.trans: Talk to Arakelyan. Get him to withdraw his statement.

meanings.note: Informal. Core Russian interj meaning 'bye' in everyday speech.
As an adverb. Core Russian interj meaning 'bye' in everyday speech.

помешать.gloss: to disturb, to interrupt; to hinder

meanings.note: Не помешал? = Am I interrupting?. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'мешать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to disturb, to interrupt; to hinder', paired with 'мешать'.

meanings.en: to get in the way, to prevent
meanings.note: + dative. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'мешать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to disturb, to interrupt; to hinder', paired with 'мешать'.

examples.trans: Nikolai Filippovich, greetings. Am I interrupting?

meanings.note: + dative. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'мочь'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to help', paired with 'помогать'.

examples.text: Экскаваторщик — это не мой уровень. Может, поможешь?
examples.trans: Excavator driver isn't my level. Maybe you could help?

meanings.note: понимаешь? = you know? do you understand?

examples.trans: I want to go to the sea, you know?

examples.text: Я хочу нормально жить! Я хочу биде, понимаешь?
examples.trans: I want to live like a normal person! I want a bidet, do you understand?

meanings.note: Понял? = got it?; понял = got it. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'нять'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to understand', paired with 'понимать'.

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'обещать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to promise', paired with 'обещать'.

examples.text: Он сегодня пообещал построить нам новое здание.
examples.trans: Today he promised to build us a new building.

examples.text: А вот Павел Юрьевич нам помог! Он сегодня пообещал построить нам новое здание.
examples.trans: Whereas Pavel Yuryevich helped us! Today he promised to build us a new building.

meanings.note: On foot, once. Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to come, to arrive', paired with 'приходить'.

examples.trans: Security will be here any moment.

examples.text: Не надо, Самсон. Сейчас придёт охрана.
examples.trans: Don't, Samson. Security will be here any second.

meanings.note: short form only: рад, рада, радо, рады; no long-form cases

examples.trans: I'm very glad to see you.

examples.text: Ну что ты? Я очень рад тебя видеть.
examples.trans: Oh, come on! I'm very glad to see you.

meanings.en: to act out, perform a scene, play a prank
meanings.note: Prefix 'раз-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (stem 'ыграть'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to play'.

examples.trans: They decided to play a trick on their friends.

examples.text: Мы разыграем один очень хитрый спектакль!
examples.trans: We will play out a very clever show!

meanings.note: рассказывай! = tell me (your news)!

examples.trans: So, tell me, how are you doing?

meanings.note: Сам, сама, само, сами. Core Russian pron meaning 'oneself (myself, yourself...)' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Я и сама хорошо проведу время.
examples.trans: I'll have a good time on my own.

meanings.note: Someone who saw what happened. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'видетель'). Agent/instrument noun formed with the productive Slavic suffix '-тель' ('-er'). Common masculine noun meaning 'witness' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: So that there are witnesses, Samson.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'коро'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Так, не шумим. Я скоро вернусь.
examples.trans: Right, no noise. I'll be back soon.

meanings.note: + accusative. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лушать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to listen', paired with 'послушать'.
the imperative 'слушай' starts a sentence, like 'look, ...'

'Слушаю' = I'm listening. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лушать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to listen', paired with 'послушать'.

examples.text: Слушай, Самсон, я тут подумал. Твой начальник — такой опытный специалист.
examples.trans: Listen, Samson, I've been thinking. Your boss is such an experienced specialist.

meanings.note: On stage. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'пектакль'). Common masculine noun meaning 'performance, play, show' in everyday Russian.
Figurative dramatic display. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'пектакль'). Common masculine noun meaning 'performance, play, show' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Аркадий Борисович, ну что же вы делаете? Прекратите этот спектакль!
examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, what are you doing? Stop this performance!

examples.text: Я не хочу играть в этот дешёвый спектакль.
examples.trans: I do not want to play in this cheap performance.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'покойно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Его не будет часа два. Вы спокойно всё сделаете.
examples.trans: He'll be gone for about two hours. You'll do everything calmly.

meanings.note: Direction. Core Russian adv meaning 'here (to this place)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: The white one? Give me the keys.

meanings.note: адвокатская тайна = attorney-client privilege

examples.text: Как? Ты?! А как же адвокатская тайна?
examples.trans: How? You?! What about lawyer-client secrecy?

meanings.note: the comparative 'тише' = quieter, used as 'shh'
тише! (comparative) = quiet! keep it down!
At that time. Core Russian adv meaning 'then, back then' in everyday speech.
Core Russian adv meaning 'then, back then' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Я тебе тогда сказал: ты меня ещё поцелуешь.
examples.trans: I told you back then: you'll kiss me one day.

meanings.note: softens a request: только не сердись = just don't be angry
Colloquial, like здесь. Core Russian adv meaning 'here' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, I'm sorry, there's a man here to see you.
